---
title: CoreWeave
description: Train on CoreWeave SUNK and publish checkpoints to Dedicated Inference
---

Axolotl integrates with CoreWeave in three ways:

- **Train on SUNK**: submit an Axolotl job to an existing SUNK (Slurm) cluster.
- **Publish checkpoints**: hot-load each saved checkpoint into a Dedicated
  Inference deployment as a compressed delta.
- **GRPO rollouts**: generate GRPO rollouts on a Dedicated Inference deployment
  instead of vLLM.

## Setup

```bash
uv pip install 'axolotl[coreweave]'
```

The container image used on SUNK must include Axolotl (and `axolotl[coreweave]`
if you publish checkpoints).

## Train on SUNK

1. Copy [`examples/cloud/coreweave.yaml`][cloud-yaml] and set your cluster details:

    ```yaml
    provider: coreweave
    ssh_host: sunk                        # omit when running on the login node
    shared_dir: /mnt/shared/axolotl-jobs
    image: /mnt/shared/images/axolotl.sqsh

    partition: h100
    nodes: 1
    gpus_per_node: 8
    # account: your-slurm-account
    # qos: your-qos
    ```

2. Submit the job:

    ```bash
    axolotl train train.yaml --cloud coreweave.yaml --launcher torchrun
    ```

3. Manage it from the login node with `squeue -j JOB_ID`, `sacct -j JOB_ID`, or
   `scancel JOB_ID`. The submit command prints the job ID and log path.

Add `dry_run: true` to the cloud YAML to preview the submission without
allocating resources.

::: {.callout-note}
- Local files are not uploaded. Datasets, checkpoints, and reward modules must be
  in the image or on shared storage (`shared_dir` or `mounts`), referenced by
  absolute paths.
- Set the topology with `nodes` and `gpus_per_node`, not launcher flags.
- Your local environment is not forwarded. For secrets such as `HF_TOKEN`, write
  `KEY=value` lines to a file on shared storage and set `env_file` to its
  absolute path; it is sourced inside the container. Set other variables (e.g.
  NCCL) under `env` in the cloud YAML.
:::

## Train on CKS

The same provider submits to a CoreWeave Kubernetes Service cluster with `backend: cks`:
one indexed Job with a pod per node, a headless Service for the rendezvous address, and a
ConfigMap carrying the training YAML and the launcher. Pods request `rdma/ib` and carry
CoreWeave's InfiniBand NCCL settings; a ReadWriteMany PVC (storage class `shared-vast`)
holds datasets, the Hugging Face cache and outputs; AI Object Storage is reached through
workload identity (a projected service-account token), so no access keys are stored.

1. Copy [`examples/cloud/coreweave-cks.yaml`](https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl/blob/main/examples/cloud/coreweave-cks.yaml) and set the namespace, PVC, node count and secrets:

    ```yaml
    provider: coreweave
    backend: cks
    image: axolotlai/axolotl-cloud:main-latest
    namespace: my-tenant-namespace
    nodes: 2
    gpus_per_node: 8
    pvc: training-shared          # mounted at /data; relative output_dir lands under /data/axolotl-jobs/<job>/
    memory_request: 1600Gi
    secret_env:
      HF_TOKEN: hf-token/token    # kubectl create secret generic hf-token --from-literal=token=...
    object_storage:
      org_id: my-org-id
      region: US-EAST-15A
    ```

2. Submit with the ambient `kubectl` context (or `kubeconfig` / `context` in the YAML):

    ```bash
    axolotl train train.yaml --cloud coreweave-cks.yaml --launcher torchrun
    ```

   The command prints the job name, a `kubectl logs -f job/<name>` line, and the delete
   command. `dry_run: true` prints the manifests instead of applying them.

::: {.callout-note}
- Topology comes from `nodes` and `gpus_per_node`; pod 0 is the rendezvous host.
- `setup_commands` run in the container before the launcher (extra wheels from the PVC, for example).
- The Hugging Face cache is pointed at `<pvc_mount>/hf` because the image pins `HF_HUB_CACHE` to the container's overlay disk; the Triton cache stays on node-local scratch, which must not be shared over NFS.
- `memory_request` has to hold the whole checkpoint in host RAM on rank 0 when `cpu_ram_efficient_loading` is on.
:::

## Publish checkpoints to Dedicated Inference

Requires an existing Dedicated Inference deployment with hot-loading enabled.
Export `CW_API_TOKEN` (an Inference Admin token) and configure AWS credentials
for CoreWeave AI Object Storage. Then add to your training config:

```yaml
plugins:
  - axolotl.integrations.coreweave.CoreWeavePlugin

coreweave:
  deployment_id: your-deployment-id
  gateway_url: https://your-gateway-endpoint
  model: your-deployment-model-name
  bucket: your-checkpoint-bucket   # must match the deployment's hot-load bucket
  path_prefix: training/run-001    # must match the deployment's hot-load prefix
  s3_profile: cw

save_safetensors: true
save_steps: 100
```

LoRA checkpoints work too (`adapter: lora` with `bf16: true`). The base model
must be an unquantized BF16 safetensors checkpoint; QLoRA, DoRA, and
`modules_to_save` are not supported.

## GRPO rollouts on Dedicated Inference

Add `rollouts: true` to the `coreweave` block above and disable vLLM:

```yaml
rl: grpo
coreweave:
  # ...deployment and storage settings from above
  rollouts: true
trl:
  use_vllm: false
  num_generations: 4
  max_completion_length: 256
  # reward_funcs as usual
```

Requirements:

- Full-model training (no adapters), text-only conversational prompts,
  synchronous GRPO.
- The deployment must use the same tokenizer and support token-ID completions
  (`return_tokens_as_token_ids`).
- Only `temperature` and `top_p` sampling are supported. Liger loss kernels and
  context parallelism are not.

## Notes

- **Delta format**: the first checkpoint is published in full, then later ones
  as [Slime-compatible][slime] XOR deltas. A new full checkpoint starts every
  `max_deltas` saves (default 128) or when the trainer restarts.
- **Background publishing**: checkpoints publish in order while training
  continues. Queued checkpoints use local disk until published. Set
  `async_publish: false` to block on each save.
- **Object storage**: do not delete the full baseline or its deltas; inference
  needs the whole chain.
- **LoRA**: each adapter is merged into the base on CPU before computing the
  delta. CPU memory scales with shard size, but local disk must hold the base
  plus merged copies.
- **Rollouts**: before each rollout round, the current weights are published and
  hot-loaded, so each round samples from the current policy.
- See [Run veRL on SUNK][verl-sunk] for shared storage and container setup, and
  [CoreWeave RL Rollouts][cw-rollouts] for deployment prerequisites and
  recovering from a failed hot-load.
